effect: Battle Mode: players start closer to the centre of the stage
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:68C4 sets $6246=1 and bit 0 of the code flags $6273/$6274; the stage builder reads $6246 ($C2:1B08). Lands on the Battle menu. The game gives it out on the "200%" screen after a second 100% clear.

effect: Battle Mode: alternate hard-block and item layout
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:68CA, $6246=2. The three layout codes (4622, 0413, 0926) share $6246, so only the last one entered counts. The game gives it out on the "200%" screen after a second 100% clear.

effect: Battle Mode: start positions moved inward with less open space
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:68D0, $6246=3. It does not unlock Gold Bomberman; Gold comes from a 100% clear, see the Gold Bomberman entry. The game itself gives it out: it is the secret password on the screen after a 100% clear, the same moment Gold is unlocked.

effect: Battle Mode: adds SUPER (スーパー) to COM LEVEL; stays unlocked
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:68E0: $6247=4 (number of COM levels) and bit 4 of $6273, which is saved to SRAM $1E8 ($C0:4858). At boot $C0:486D restores $6247=4 from that bit.

effect: Battle Mode: every soft block holds a power-up
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:6997, bit 5 of $6274.

effect: Normal Mode: start with 8 bombs, 8 fire, top speed, remote control, kick and power glove
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:6928, bit 3 of $6274; the stage script reads it ($C2:1ACB) and gives the full-power start ($C4:2926): $17CA=8 bombs, $4EBD=8 fire, speed $15EA:$15D2=$0200 (normal $00E0), and $4ED5=$07 = remote control (bit 0, bomb fuse $0E40=$FF, $C4:3059), kick (bit 1) and power glove (bit 2). Round 1 read $4ED5 as speed; it is the item bitfield. In play (A drops a bomb) the fuse $0E40 stayed $FF for 300 frames and B set it off; kick and glove were not tried in play.

effect: Normal Mode: 9 lives and an 8:00 stage timer
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:69A9, bit 6 of $6274; the timer is picked at $C5:03A9 (8 or 3 minutes). The HUD showed 9 lives and 7:58.

effect: Boss rush: the Normal Mode bosses one after another
note: Option > PASSWORD (4 digits). Handler $C5:695E: mode $67 with $6254=0 (normal starting power). Starts straight in a boss arena. Bit 7 of $6274 also stops the game saving.

code: Super Joycard turbo X on the title screen
effect: Unlock battle stages 11-13 (kept in SRAM $1EA)
note: Holding X with the Joycard's turbo on is what works: $C1:75F9 counts new X presses on any pad. It needs 39-54 presses in 360 frames (6 s) with no gap of 16 frames or more. That means a 6.5-9 Hz turbo or fast tapping; holding X does nothing. Verified with 8-frame and 4-frame-on/4-off turbo (works), and with 4-frame turbo, 12-frame turbo and plain holding (fail). The Caravan ROM unlocks the stages at boot without this.

effect: Gold Bomberman joins the Battle Mode character select (replacing the random X)
note: The end-of-game certificate script ($C6:E07D) unlocks him if the clear rate in $103C is 100: script native 67 ($C0:4880) writes 1 to SRAM $1E9. Native 68 ($C0:4893) reads it at character select. Tested both halves: forcing 100 wrote the flag, and setting the flag showed him. First, the 100% screen shows the secret password 0926, sets the per-file 100% count $6258 and clears all 100 progress flags; a second 100% shows "200%" with 4622 and 0413 (BizHawk, Japan and English, flags set in memory).

effect: Invincibility (the hit timer never runs out)
note: The flag that the orphaned password handler $C5:6951 would have set; $C4:2D2B reads it. Bomberman survived his own blast in Normal Mode with it held at 1. Caravan address is 7E6271 (not tested). Round 3: run through Mesen's PAR cheat engine on retail and English: the player survives his own bomb at the start of 1-1 (without it he dies). Caravan: 7E6271:01. Game Genie: $C4:2D2F BNE -> BRA, the branch taken when $6253 is set; Mesen, retail and English: the player survives his own bomb at the start of 1-1.

effect: Config Battle editor: body 9 (Subordinate Bomber) / color 7 (boss palette)
note: In retail the editor block is $1F lower than in the Caravan (gold) cartridge (7E62FD/7E62FE there); the decoder writes body/color to $62DE/$62DF. The editor variables were found in Mesen by cycling body/color; the PAR values themselves weren't tested.

effect: Debug room $AC (battle test): Zone 3 mine layout, players only, no music
note: Needs patches/sb5_debug_rooms.ips (tools/sb5/make_ips.py). Typed with real presses on the patched ROM. The patch copies the option password table to $C5:6FA0 and adds 0172/0173/0174. Scene $AC runs $C7:170D.

effect: Debug room $AD (level test): battle stage 1 layout, two enemies, soft blocks with items
note: Needs patches/sb5_debug_rooms.ips. Scene $AD runs the room script at $C6:0309 (scene n uses entry n-1 of the table at $C6:0000).

effect: Debug room $AE (enemy test): one enemy, broken HUD
note: Needs patches/sb5_debug_rooms.ips. Scene $AE runs $C6:03B8, the last entry of the scene table; the HUD is broken and the screen goes black about 10 s in.

effect: PAR room/scene select: the next valid option password goes to scene xx (AC, AD, AE = debug rooms; 0D-66 stages, 67-70 bosses, 74-A7 battle stages)
note: $6248 is the scene run after the password screen (it becomes $1031). Round 3: verified with Mesen's cheat engine on retail and English with AC, AD and 2B after 4622. The known 7E1038:XX is a shared work byte. Caravan: same address ($6245-$6248 don't move); Mesen's cheat engine with 4622: AC gives the debug battle-test room, 2B zone 3-1 and 74 battle stage 1.

effect: Invincibility (Caravan address of 7E6253)
note: Mesen PAR cheat engine: the player survives his own bomb at the start of 1-1. Caravan WRAM from $6249 up is $1E higher. Game Genie: the same BNE -> BRA at Caravan $C4:2D70; Mesen: the player survives his own bomb at the start of 1-1.

effect: Invincibility and the stage clock stops
note: $0E23 is tested at $C4:2D31 (hit check, right after $6253) and $C5:0460 (skips the clock tick $0E1C-$0E1E); no code ever sets it (only STZ at $C5:0404). Verified with Mesen's cheat engine on all three ROMs: survives own bomb, clock frozen. Game Genie: BNE -> BRA after both $0E23 tests ($C4:2D2F, Caravan $C4:2D70; $C5:0469); Mesen on all three ROMs: survives his own bomb, clock frozen.

effect: Gold Bomberman on the Battle character select without a 100% clear
note: Patches the read of SRAM $1E9 (native 68, $C0:4893 LDA $3061E9; Caravan $C0:4899). Verified on retail with Mesen's cheat engine (Gold in the bottom-right slot, SRAM itself stays 0); Caravan and English use the same instruction but were not run. Game Genie: LDA $3061E9 -> LDA #$01 + NOP NOP at $C0:4893 (Caravan $C0:4899); Mesen on all three ROMs: Gold Bomberman in the bottom-right slot of the character select.

effect: Battle stages 11-13 without the Super Joycard
note: $6245 = number of battle stages (10 or 13). Verified with Mesen's cheat engine on retail and English ($6245=13 at the Battle menu). Caravan has them unlocked already. The known 7E625A:0B-0D picks the stage instead. Game Genie: the LDA #$0A before STA $7E6245 ($C0:48C3) loads 13; Mesen, retail and English: $6245=13 at the Battle menu.

effect: 3879 boss rush starts fully powered (8 bombs, 8 fire, top speed, remote, kick, glove): 0719 on retail
note: ROM code: the operand of LDA #$00 / STA $6254 in the 3879 handler ($C5:6982). A RAM code is too late because 3879 builds the players in the same frame. Verified with Mesen's cheat engine: $17CA=8, $4EBD=8, $15EA=2, $4ED5=7 in the boss arena (without it 2/1/0/0). Game Genie: the same ROM byte; Mesen with 3879, retail and English: $17CA=8, $4EBD=8, $15EA=2, $4ED5=7 in the boss arena.

code: Battle rules: みそボン, Right from スーパー (Caravan)
effect: A fourth Misobon setting, ハイパー (HYPER): a Misobon player who blows someone up comes back with that player's bombs, fire and speed
note: Caravan adds bit $40 to the rules byte ($7E627B; retail $7E625D uses $10 スーパー and $08 ON) and a HYPER case to the menu script ($C6:9187, label graphic $83), so the row cycles ハイパー, スーパー, ON, OFF; in retail Right on スーパー does nothing. $C4:37F9 saves each player's stats when they die ($4EBD bombs, $17CA fire, $15EA speed, $15D2, $4ED5), $C4:37EB records who made a Misobon kill, and with HYPER $C4:3822 hands the killer the victim's saved stats on return. In Mesen (5-player Battle Royale, the setting chosen in the menu): the returning player got the victim's 5 bombs, fire 6 (7 when the victim had picked up a fire-up) and speed 3, against 1 / 2 / 1 with スーパー. Image: Caravan (left) and retail after the same press.

effect: A cut computer-only battle: all five fighters play themselves, the clock starts at 3:00 and Start can't pause
note: $1D1C is only ever cleared ($C0:31BF); no instruction or script writes it, and the attract demos don't use it. When set: $C4:0074 sets $1D26 = 1, $C4:2A08 makes every player a computer (type 2), $C5:0E11 sets the time byte $625C = 2 and $C5:0046 skips the pause check. Held at 1 in Mesen while warping into battle room $74: within 120 frames all five fighters move and bomb on their own (in the normal battle nobody has moved yet); the round plays out to the time-up block fill, then sits at 0:28 with no results screen. Image: normal battle at 120 frames (left), the computer-only battle at 120 frames, and later in the round. Caravan: the same five reads ($C4:006F, $C4:2A39, $C5:0046, $C5:0E22, $C5:3C09) and only the clear at $C0:31C5; held at 1 in Mesen while warping into room $74: $1D26 = 1, the clock starts at 3:00 and all fighters play themselves. English is static (the same code at the same addresses).

code: Text menus from before the graphic ones
effect: About 30 menus written in plain kana that the finished game draws as pictures instead, one of them reading "under construction: the Bowling Bomber goes here"
note: Windows of text table 4 ($D1:0000): the file menu ($08, $0A, $0B), game over ($52, $53), the battle and Config Bomber menus ($4A-$4E, $5C-$62), the rules ($55), Maniac settings ($56-$58), stage and teams ($59-$5B), the bowling prizes ($B3) and $B4, コウジチュウ / ココニハ ボーリングボンバー ガ ハイリマス. They need one font no scene loads (group 3, set 11, $D3:A7AC). No code produces any of them: every store of a message number was enumerated, including the script's stack calls (op $4A), and a BizHawk run through the menus logged every message drawn without one appearing. Shown in BizHawk through the game's own drawer, forced onto the Battle Mode scene, so the palette and the cursor are that scene's. A second trace through game over, the zone maps, the file and password screens, every Config Bomber screen, Bowling Bomber, the certificate and both endings drew none of them either.

effect: Stage labels A2, A3, B2, E2 and J2 that no zone map uses
note: Messages $39, $3A, $3C, $40 and $46 of text table 4. The boss nodes' labels ($38, $3B, $3D-$3F, $41-$45) read A to J; these five belong to node ids ($20, $21, $23, $27, $2D) that are in none of the six node tables ($C2:1070). Drawn in BizHawk by the game's own drawer in the zone 1 map header, in place of the label of stage 1.

code: Unused item icons and battle counts
effect: Eight more item icons in the Config Bomber style (vest, clock, Bomberman face, skulls, a heart...) and BATTLE counts 6 to 9
note: Text table 6. $06-$09 are the digits 6-9 after the rules screen's BATTLE count, which stops at 5. $B0-$B3, $B7 and $BB-$BD are 16x16 item icons beside the nine the ability screen uses (its table $C6:7F37 lists only those). Also unused: a dash for the file screen's clear rate ($C8) and the editor's hiragana set as two sheets ($A2, $AC). Each drawn in BizHawk by the game's own drawer in place of a used neighbour on its own screen.
